profile.campus: Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon (QTS Hillsboro 3 campus)
profile.address: 23615 NE Schaaf St, North Hillsboro, OR 97124
profile.reading:
Per Data Center Dynamics' 2020 coverage of QTS's Hillsboro 3 campus opening, this North Hillsboro site (reverse-geocoded to 23615 NE Schaaf St, a separate parcel from the Pubols Street building tracked elsewhere in this registry) is part of the same mega-scale campus first announced in 2018, planned for five data centers totaling 250+ MW across more than 1 million sq ft; Phase 1 opened October 2, 2020 with a 158,000 sq ft building and 24 MW of capacity, following a February 2020 groundbreaking on a 27MW phase.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. Hillsboro, in Oregon's Washington County, is one of three QTS campuses in the immediate area (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3) and part of the Portland metro's broader "Silicon Forest" data center cluster, drawing power from the regional grid and, per QTS's own Hillsboro 3 materials, offering customers 100% renewable energy through power purchase agreements.

Hillsboro's "Silicon Forest" data center cluster grew out of the area's legacy semiconductor and electronics manufacturing base (anchored historically by Intel's large Washington County campuses), which left behind substantial fiber infrastructure and a skilled technical workforce that later attracted data center operators; the Hillsboro Herald, a local outlet, has reported on the scale of competing data center construction projects in the immediate area as the industrial land base has shifted from chip fabrication toward digital infrastructure. QTS's Hillsboro presence, spread across three separate campuses (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3), reflects a broader industry pattern in Oregon's Washington County of sequential campus expansion by the same operator as adjacent land becomes available, similar to the multi-campus patterns seen for QTS in Northern Virginia and for other operators in this registry's Loudoun County and Quincy, Washington clusters.

reading.body:
QTS Data Center - Hillsboro 3 is a planned campus in Oregon's largest data center hub, designed as a two-building, 44-acre complex with 100+ MW total power capacity. The operator has not published specific building addresses or per-building power allocations, and the facility remains in development. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, typical for AI training workloads, 100 MW of IT load would support roughly 2,500 racks. At an assumed 6 to 8 accelerators per rack at current densities, this translates to a potential base for 15,000 to 20,000 GPUs, though the actual split between training, inference, and other workloads is not published.

Oregon has published power specifications for only eight data center facilities totaling 156.6 MW across 133 mapped sites, meaning most large facilities in the state do not disclose capacity. If and when Hillsboro 3 completes, its 100+ MW would rank it roughly ninth among published Oregon capacities by that preliminary measure, though this ranking reflects only disclosed figures and will shift as other operators publish. Hillsboro as a region hosts Digital Realty, Verizon, and other major operators, establishing it as a multi-tenant hub rather than a single operator's territory.

Certifications and tenant commitments for this specific campus are not published. The facility's relevance to AI scaling depends entirely on when it comes online and what its actual per-building power distribution enables, neither of which the operator has disclosed. Until construction details and live power commitments emerge, this campus cannot yet be counted as available capacity for AI workloads.
